title: Fluctuation theorems for autonomous work in the quantum regime
abstract: Fluctuation theorems for work provide universal constraints on nonequilibrium fluctuations, yet their quantum generalizations often rely on externally prescribed classical driving protocols. While for classical systems, fluctuation theorems have been extended to autonomous work, where the dynamics of the work source is subject to the backaction of the system, their generalization to the quantum regime is constrained by the uncertainty principle. Here, we extend fluctuation theorems for autonomous work from the classical regime to the quantum regime. By performing successive projective measurements over the work source and the system, we derive Jarzynski-type and Crooks-type fluctuation theorems for autonomous inclusive work from initial mixed thermal states. These relations are analogous to fluctuation theorems for autonomous work in the classical regime and explicitly incorporate the fluctuations of the work source. However, quantum noncommutativity prevents a consistent reduction to the nonautonomous counterparts, even in the limit of a large work source and correspondingly negligible backaction. By contrast, under the exclusive work definition, the nonautonomous limit is recovered when the measured observable of the work source commutes with its bare Hamiltonian and the backaction of the system on the work source is negligible. Our results are illustrated with the Dicke model, where a single-mode radiation field and an ensemble of two-level atoms act as the system of interest and the work source, respectively.
summary: This paper extends fluctuation theorems for autonomous work from classical physics into the quantum regime. It derives generalized Jarzynski and Crooks relations using projective measurements on a coupled system. The key finding is that quantum noncommutativity imposes fundamental constraints, preventing simple reduction to classical forms, which is demonstrated using the Dicke model.
main_problem: The primary goal is extending fluctuation theorems for autonomous work from classical statistical mechanics into the quantum domain.
main_result: Fluctuation theorems (Jarzynski-type and Crooks-type) are derived for inclusive work, showing that quantum noncommutativity prevents a simple reduction to nonautonomous forms.
method: The authors use successive projective measurements over the work source and system Hamiltonian to derive generalized fluctuation relations by comparing forward and backward process probabilities.
model_or_system: The analysis is generally framed for a composite system ($S$ coupled to $R$), but the Dicke model (single-mode radiation field as system, two-level atoms as work source) is used for concrete illustration.
key_observables: Inclusive work ($w[\Gamma]$), joint probabilities ($P_F[\Gamma], P_B[	ilde{\Gamma}]$), and fluctuation variables $R$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the work source observable has a discrete spectrum; crucially, quantum noncommutativity prevents a direct reduction to nonautonomous fluctuation theorems.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general measurement framework. Figure 2 and 8 confirm the Crooks-type theorem in the Dicke model by showing the collapse of $P_F$ and $P_B e^R$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical extension of fluctuation theorems for autonomous work to the quantum regime, derives the relations using measurement formalism, discusses the constraints imposed by quantum mechanics (noncommutativity), and verifies these results using the Dicke model.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium thermodynamics in open quantum systems, which is central to understanding energy transduction in nanoscale quantum devices and quantum heat engines.
